Is the Options Market Predicting a Spike in CDW Stock?
Tue, September 29, 2026 at 7:13 AM PDT 2 min read
Investors in CDW, Inc. CDW need to pay close attention to the stock based on moves in the options market lately. That is because the October 16, 2026 $175.00 Put had some of the highest implied volatility of all equity options today.
What is Implied Volatility?
Implied volatility shows how much movement the market is expecting in the future. Options with high levels of implied volatility suggest that investors in the underlying stocks are expecting a big move in one direction or the other. It could also mean there is an event coming up soon that may cause a big rally or a huge sell off. However, implied volatility is only one piece of the puzzle when putting together an options trading strategy.
What do the Analysts Think?
Clearly, options traders are pricing in a big move for CDW, but what is the fundamental picture for the company? Currently, CDW is a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) in the Computers - IT Services Industry that ranks in the Top 27% of our Zacks Industry Rank. Over the last 60 days, three analysts have increased their estimates for the current quarter, while one has revised his estimate downward. The net effect has taken our Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current quarter to move from $2.91 per share to $2.92 per share in the same time period.
Given the way analysts feel about CDW right now, this huge implied volatility could mean there's a trade developing. Often times, options traders look for options with high levels of implied volatility to sell premium. This is a strategy many seasoned traders use because it captures decay. At expiration, the hope for these traders is that the underlying stock does not move as much as originally expected.

CDW Canada’s AI Workplace Trends Report Finds Canadian Organizations Entering New Phase of AI Maturity as Agentic AI Gains Ground
New research shows AI is moving beyond experimentation in Canadian workplaces, but trust, training and measurement remain critical barriers to realizing business outcomes.
ETOBICOKE, Ontario, September 22, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Today, CDW Canada, the strategic end-to-end technology partner that turns customer ambition into outcomes, released new research exploring how Canadian organizations are moving from artificial intelligence (AI) deployment to realizing business value. The report, Canada's AI Workplace Evolution from Adoption to Accountability, draws on a survey conducted by Earnscliffe on behalf of CDW Canada of 1,011 Canadian office workers across organizations of varying sizes and industries throughout Canada.
The report finds AI is now firmly embedded in Canadian workplaces, with daily use of workplace-approved AI tools nearly doubling year over year (31 percent, up from 18 percent). But as adoption becomes mainstream, organizations are increasingly focused on a more pressing challenge: turning AI investments into measurable business outcomes. The research also points to the rapid rise of agentic AI, with one third of employees already reporting the use of AI agents capable of completing multistep workflows, making recommendations and helping drive outcomes.
"AI adoption is no longer the story," said KJ Burke, Field CTO, Hybrid Infrastructure, CDW Canada. "Most organizations have moved beyond asking whether employees will use AI. The question now is whether those investments are creating meaningful business value. The organizations that lead in the years ahead will be the ones that can measure impact, build trust and reimagine how work gets done by empowering employees to work effectively with AI systems."
The next phase of workplace AI is already taking shape, signalling a shift from AI tools that assist with individual tasks to systems that can help execute more complex workflows and contribute to outcomes.
The research suggests organizations are beginning to move from simply consuming AI technologies to actively shaping them. Nearly one-in-three agentic AI users report their organization is already building AI agents in-house.
At the same time, the findings highlight the importance of employee enablement. Workers who receive hands-on AI training report significantly higher levels of confidence using AI (46 percent are very confident) than those who receive no formal support (23 percent), underscoring the growing need for practical, role-specific training as AI capabilities become more advanced.
"Agentic AI represents an important shift in how organizations think about AI," said KJ Burke, Field CTO, Hybrid Infrastructure, CDW Canada. "As AI evolves from assisting employees to helping execute work, organizations must invest not only in technology, but also in the skills, governance and trust required to use it responsibly and effectively."
Trust remains the biggest obstacle to deeper AI adoption
Employee attitudes toward AI continue to trend positively. Curiosity remains the dominant sentiment among workers (42 percent) and outweighs the percentage that are worried about AI, suggesting employees are increasingly open to AI in the workplace.
However, trust continues to be a barrier to broader and deeper adoption. Accuracy and reliability are among the top AI concerns across daily users (31 percent), less frequent users (24 percent) and those not yet using approved tools (43 percent).
The findings also show that barriers vary depending on an employee's experience with AI. More advanced users tend to focus on privacy and security concerns, while those who have yet to embrace AI are more likely to question both its reliability and its relevance to their role.
"The challenge for organizations is no longer generating interest in AI," said Ashley Otto, Senior Product Manager, CDW Canada. "It's helping employees trust the technology enough to use it confidently and effectively. That requires clear governance, practical use cases and ongoing education."
Organizations are beginning to see value, but many still struggle to measure it
The research suggests AI is delivering benefits beyond simple efficiency gains. Compared to 2025, employees with access to AI at work increasingly report improvements in productivity (58 percent, up 11 points), quality of outputs (54 percent, up 15 points) and innovation (48 percent, up 11 points), indicating that organizations are beginning to realize broader business value from AI investments.
Despite this progress, many organizations continue to face a measurement gap. While more organizations report tracking specific KPIs to evaluate AI performance than they did a year ago (38 percent, up from 24 percent), a significant number still lack formal frameworks to assess ROI (23 percent) or are unsure whether such measurement exists (23 percent).
As AI programs mature and investment scrutiny intensifies, the ability to measure and communicate impact is critical to ensuring effective adoption. For CDW Canada, that means helping organizations move beyond AI implementation to building sustainable programs grounded in strategy, employee enablement, governance and measurable business outcomes.
"Most organizations can tell you how many employees have access to AI," said Burke. "Far fewer can clearly demonstrate what AI has changed for their business. We're entering an accountability phase where success will be defined not by access or experimentation, but by an organization's ability to prove value and sustain results."
For Canadian organizations, the next phase of AI success will be defined by trust, workforce readiness and measurable outcomes. As organizations explore emerging technologies such as agentic AI, CDW Canada is helping customers build the strategies, skills and governance frameworks needed to turn AI investments into lasting business value.
To learn more about the state of AI in Canadian workplaces, download the full 2026 Canadian AI Workspace Trends Report: Canada's AI Workplace Evolution from Adoption to Accountability.
Join the conversation online by following @CDWCanada on X and LinkedIn.
This study was conducted by Earnscliffe on behalf of CDW Canada. Earnscliffe is a member of CRIC and abides by the ESOMAR code of Market, Opinion, and Social Research and Data Analytics and CRIC standards, including the CRIC Public Opinion Research Standards and Disclosure Requirements.
The online survey was in field from June 15 to 25, 2026, with a sample of 1,011 Canadian office workers who work in organizations with at least 20 employees and use a computer in an office setting 11 or more hours a week, using Leger's LEO panel. Quotas were set for business size, sector, region, age and gender to align with sample structure from previous waves, and data is unweighted.
The survey was conducted in English. Online surveys cannot be assigned a margin of error.
CDW Canada Corp. is the strategic end-to-end technology partner that cuts through complexity to turn customer ambition into outcomes. Working with organizations across the business, government, education and healthcare sectors, CDW enables organizations to navigate an increasingly complex technology market and turn their technology investments into lasting value. CDW Canada is a wholly owned subsidiary of CDW Corporation (Nasdaq: CDW), a global organization. For more information, visit CDW.ca.

Amkor Technology Announces Phase 2 of Arizona Advanced Packaging and Test Campus; Expands Investment to $12 Billion
Strong customer commitments support 60,000 square meter expansion of U.S. advanced packaging capacity
TEMPE, Ariz.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Sep. 8, 2026--
Amkor Technology, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMKR), a leading provider of outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services, today announced phase 2 of its Arizona Advanced packaging and test campus. Driven by strong customer commitments that have surpassed the 33,000 square meters of cleanroom capacity planned for phase 1, the phase 2 expansion is expected to add 60,000 square meters and bring the campus to approximately 93,000 square meters of cleanroom space. The expansion increases the project’s planned investment to approximately $12 billion.
Designed from the outset as a multi-phase project, Amkor’s Arizona campus, which includes wafer bump, probe, assembly and test capabilities, is being developed to support long-term demand for advanced semiconductor packaging and test services in the U.S. Phase 2 expands manufacturing scale, and together with phase 1 is expected to support a workforce of more than 3,500 Arizona-based employees.
“This next phase reflects the confidence our customers have placed in Amkor, the critical role advanced packaging plays in enabling the future of semiconductor innovation, and the strategic importance of our Arizona campus,” said Kevin Engel, president and chief executive officer of Amkor Technology. “As chip architectures become more complex, customers need a trusted partner that can deliver at scale with the quality, technology leadership and operational discipline required for their most advanced products, and it is critical to have that capacity in the U.S.”
Amkor’s Arizona campus is the first OSAT production site in the U.S. for advanced packaging in high volume, giving customers access to a full domestic turnkey manufacturing platform. Construction of phase 2 is anticipated to begin late 2027, with completion expected by the end of 2029. Amkor’s Arizona 170-acre campus allows for further expansion as needed to support customer demand.
About Amkor Technology, Inc.
Amkor Technology, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMKR) is the world’s largest U.S. headquartered OSAT and is a global leader in outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services. With a strong track record of innovation, a broad and diverse geographic footprint and solid partnerships with lead customers, Amkor delivers high-quality solutions that enable the world’s leading semiconductor and electronics companies to bring advanced technologies to market. The company’s comprehensive portfolio includes advanced packaging, wafer-level processing, and system-in-package solutions targeting applications for smartphones, data centers, artificial intelligence, automobiles and wearables. For more information visit amkor.com.

Amkor vs. AXT: Which Semiconductor Stock Is the Better Buy Now?
Amkor Technology AMKR is a major outsourced semiconductor assembly and test provider, offering advanced packaging solutions for AI, high-performance computing, automotive and communications markets. AXT, Inc. AXTI manufactures compound-semiconductor substrates, including indium phosphide and gallium arsenide, which are used in optical communications and other high-performance applications.
Although the companies serve different parts of the semiconductor supply chain, both are benefiting from rising investment in AI infrastructure. Amkor recently reported record second-quarter 2026 revenues and is expanding its advanced-packaging capacity, while AXT posted record quarterly indium phosphide revenues amid strong data-center optical demand. These developments make AMKR and AXTI an interesting comparison for investors seeking exposure to semiconductor and AI-infrastructure growth.
But which stock offers greater upside potential today? Let's compare the companies' recent performance, growth opportunities and key risks to see how AMKR and AXTI stack up.
Amkor offers exposure to the semiconductor supply chain through outsourced semiconductor packaging and test (OSAT), with advanced packaging becoming increasingly important as AI and high-performance computing (HPC) chips grow more complex. The company's second-quarter 2026 results showed this opportunity gaining traction: revenues reached a record $1.9 billion, up 26% year over year, while gross margin expanded to 16.8% from 12% and net income attributable to Amkor rose to $174 million from $54 million.
Growth prospects are increasingly tied to AI/HPC and advanced packaging. Amkor has active programs spanning 2.5D, high-density fan-out and co-packaged optics, while a new data-center CPU program began ramping in the second quarter and is expected to scale through the second half. Computing revenues rose 20% sequentially in the second quarter and were expected to increase nearly 30% sequentially in the third quarter, driven by AI data-center demand and the HDFO CPU ramp. Automotive & Industrial revenues advanced 17% sequentially, with ADAS the primary growth driver.
Strategic customer agreements strengthen the opportunity. A 10-year advanced-packaging agreement with TSMC is designed to expand U.S. packaging and test capacity, while a multi-year NVIDIA partnership targets next-generation AI infrastructure. Amkor expects a $1.5 billion NVIDIA-related customer prepayment in 2027, with services expected to extend roughly five to 10 years. Its Arizona facility is intended to provide high-volume advanced packaging and test capacity in the United States, while expansions in Korea, Vietnam, Portugal and Taiwan increase geographic flexibility.
However, investors should weigh these opportunities against Amkor's semiconductor cyclicality, heavy capital requirements, customer concentration, supply-chain and memory constraints, intense OSAT competition and dependence on sustained AI/HPC packaging demand. The company spent $688 million on capital expenditures in the first half and expects $2.5-$3 billion for 2026. Therefore, a slowdown in AI infrastructure investment could lead to excess capacity, lower utilization and pricing pressure.
AXT is benefiting from strong demand for compound-semiconductor substrates as AI data centers increase their use of high-speed optical connectivity. In the second quarter of 2026, revenues surged 164.8% year over year to $47.6 million, while GAAP gross margin expanded to 44.9% from 8% and GAAP net income reached $11.1 million, versus a $7 million loss a year earlier. Substrate revenues rose 232.7% to $37.6 million, driven primarily by InP demand for data centers and passive optical networks.
The strongest opportunity is indium phosphide (InP), which is emerging as the company's primary growth driver. Second-quarter InP revenues reached a record $30.7 million, while backlog exceeded $100 million. Management said customer demand continues to outpace supply and expects InP revenue opportunity to more than triple by year-end 2026. AXT is doubling InP capacity in 2026, plans another major expansion in 2027 and is progressing toward 6-inch InP substrates, which can support higher-value applications. Demand is being driven by 800G/1.6T transceivers and longer-term co-packaged optics.
AXT has recently deepened relationships with key optical-component customers supporting AI data-center connectivity. It has secured supply agreements with Casela and Coherent and a long-term capacity reservation agreement with Lumentum. These agreements provide greater revenue visibility, validate strong customer demand and support AXT's capacity expansion.
Despite AXT's strong growth prospects, its outlook remains exposed to several operational and geopolitical risks. The company manufactures its wafer substrates in China, making its business vulnerable to changing export controls, tariffs and trade restrictions. Notably, China's export-permit requirement for InP wafers remains a significant concern and can affect the timing of shipments and revenue recognition. AXT also faces semiconductor demand cyclicality, customer order volatility and the risk that major customers reduce, delay or cancel orders. In addition, maintaining high wafer yields and meeting stringent customer specifications are critical, as quality issues can lead to product returns, lower orders and higher manufacturing costs.
How Does the Zacks Consensus Estimate Compare for AMKR & AXTI?
The Zacks Consensus Estimate for AMKR's 2026 and 2027 revenues stands at $7.64 billion and $8.55 billion, respectively, giving Amkor a significantly larger revenue base than AXT. The consensus mark for AMKR's 2026 and 2027 earnings is pegged at $2.60 and $2.72 per share, implying growth of 73.3% and 4.3%, respectively. The earnings estimates have remained stable over the past seven days.
In comparison, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for AXTI's 2026 and 2027 revenues stands at $217.6 million and $453.6 million, respectively. The consensus mark for AXTI's 2026 and 2027 earnings is pegged at 86 cents and $2.20 per share, indicating 309.8% and 155.8% growth, respectively. AXTI's earnings estimates have also remained unchanged over the past seven days.
AMKR vs. AXTI: Price Performance & Valuation Check
AMKR has outpaced AXTI over the past month, with its shares gaining 9.8% compared with a 7.7% rise for AXTI, reflecting stronger recent momentum.
From a valuation perspective, AMKR appears more attractively valued than AXTI. Amkor carries a more favorable Zacks Value Score of B, compared with AXTI's value score of F. AMKR also trades at a forward 12-month price-to-sales ratio of 1.6X, significantly below AXTI's 12.26X.
Amkor and AXT are both positioned to benefit from growing AI infrastructure spending, with AMKR benefiting from advanced packaging demand and AXTI from strong InP substrate demand for optical connectivity. AMKR's growth is supported by expanding AI/HPC packaging programs, strategic partnerships and capacity expansion across key manufacturing locations. AXTI, meanwhile, has a strong InP growth opportunity, supported by record revenues, a growing backlog and capacity expansion plans, but remains more exposed to external factors, including geopolitical and customer-related risks.
However, Amkor's stronger revenue scale, more diversified business, favorable valuation and solid earnings outlook make it a better pick for investors than AXTI, though both stocks sport a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) at present.

Amkor Technology Announces Phase 2 of Arizona Advanced Packaging and Test Campus; Expands Investment to $12 Billion
Strong customer commitments support 60,000 square meter expansion of U.S. advanced packaging capacity
TEMPE, Ariz.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Sep. 8, 2026--
Amkor Technology, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMKR), a leading provider of outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services, today announced phase 2 of its Arizona Advanced packaging and test campus. Driven by strong customer commitments that have surpassed the 33,000 square meters of cleanroom capacity planned for phase 1, the phase 2 expansion is expected to add 60,000 square meters and bring the campus to approximately 93,000 square meters of cleanroom space. The expansion increases the project’s planned investment to approximately $12 billion.
Designed from the outset as a multi-phase project, Amkor’s Arizona campus, which includes wafer bump, probe, assembly and test capabilities, is being developed to support long-term demand for advanced semiconductor packaging and test services in the U.S. Phase 2 expands manufacturing scale, and together with phase 1 is expected to support a workforce of more than 3,500 Arizona-based employees.
“This next phase reflects the confidence our customers have placed in Amkor, the critical role advanced packaging plays in enabling the future of semiconductor innovation, and the strategic importance of our Arizona campus,” said Kevin Engel, president and chief executive officer of Amkor Technology. “As chip architectures become more complex, customers need a trusted partner that can deliver at scale with the quality, technology leadership and operational discipline required for their most advanced products, and it is critical to have that capacity in the U.S.”
Amkor’s Arizona campus is the first OSAT production site in the U.S. for advanced packaging in high volume, giving customers access to a full domestic turnkey manufacturing platform. Construction of phase 2 is anticipated to begin late 2027, with completion expected by the end of 2029. Amkor’s Arizona 170-acre campus allows for further expansion as needed to support customer demand.
About Amkor Technology, Inc.
Amkor Technology, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMKR) is the world’s largest U.S. headquartered OSAT and is a global leader in outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services. With a strong track record of innovation, a broad and diverse geographic footprint and solid partnerships with lead customers, Amkor delivers high-quality solutions that enable the world’s leading semiconductor and electronics companies to bring advanced technologies to market. The company’s comprehensive portfolio includes advanced packaging, wafer-level processing, and system-in-package solutions targeting applications for smartphones, data centers, artificial intelligence, automobiles and wearables. For more information visit amkor.com.

Is Amkor Technology (AMKR) Arizona Expansion A Turning Point For Its U.S. Growth?
Amkor Technology (NasdaqGS:AMKR) announced phase 2 of its Arizona advanced packaging and test campus expansion, driven by strong customer demand.
The enlarged site is set to operate as the first high volume U.S. OSAT production facility dedicated to advanced semiconductor packaging.
The project increases Amkor's planned investment and workforce in Arizona while supporting domestic supply chains for advanced chip packaging services.
The phase 2 Arizona campus buildout matters. However, investors should weigh it alongside Amkor's broader risks and fundamentals. Check out 2 warning signs that Amkor Technology investors should know about.
Rising interest in advanced packaging and domestic chip capacity makes it worth exploring related AI infrastructure exposure through 88 AI infrastructure stocks.
NasdaqGS:AMKR Earnings & Revenue Growth as at Sep 2026
Amkor Technology runs outsourced semiconductor packaging and test operations across the US, Japan, Europe, and the Asia Pacific, giving it a global footprint behind many chipmakers you know by name. The enlarged Arizona campus extends that footprint inside the US supply chain for advanced packaging services.
5 things going right for Amkor Technology that this headline doesn't cover.
How Amkor Technology's Arizona buildout pressures both the bull and bear stories
The investment story around Amkor Technology hinges on whether heavy spending on advanced packaging across regions can translate into higher value production rather than underused factories. The Arizona expansion drops right into the middle of that bet, since it both supports long-term customer programs and raises the bar for execution.
"Expansion of Amkor Technology's global footprint in Arizona, Korea, Vietnam, Portugal and Taiwan is designed to match customer needs for regional supply chains and advanced packaging...
See how the full story points towards a $76.40 fair value for Amkor Technology.
The phase 2 Arizona build fits the bullish Narrative that Amkor Technology can secure long-duration, AI-driven packaging work by offering local, high volume capacity to partners like TSMC and NVIDIA. It also strengthens the pitch against OSAT rivals such as ASE and JCET that lean more heavily on Asian sites.
The bear side is not erased though. This project magnifies the existing concern that underutilized U.S. manufacturing could pressure margins if loading lags, especially with US$12b now tied to one campus. Execution on customer ramps, mix and pricing will largely determine whether that risk or the footprint thesis wins out.
The same Arizona announcement can read as either validation of a regional advanced-packaging story or as a leverage point for capacity and margin worries, depending on which Narrative you lean toward.

Amkor vs. AXT: Which Semiconductor Stock Is the Better Buy Now?
Amkor Technology AMKR is a major outsourced semiconductor assembly and test provider, offering advanced packaging solutions for AI, high-performance computing, automotive and communications markets. AXT, Inc. AXTI manufactures compound-semiconductor substrates, including indium phosphide and gallium arsenide, which are used in optical communications and other high-performance applications.
Although the companies serve different parts of the semiconductor supply chain, both are benefiting from rising investment in AI infrastructure. Amkor recently reported record second-quarter 2026 revenues and is expanding its advanced-packaging capacity, while AXT posted record quarterly indium phosphide revenues amid strong data-center optical demand. These developments make AMKR and AXTI an interesting comparison for investors seeking exposure to semiconductor and AI-infrastructure growth.
But which stock offers greater upside potential today? Let's compare the companies' recent performance, growth opportunities and key risks to see how AMKR and AXTI stack up.
Amkor offers exposure to the semiconductor supply chain through outsourced semiconductor packaging and test (OSAT), with advanced packaging becoming increasingly important as AI and high-performance computing (HPC) chips grow more complex. The company's second-quarter 2026 results showed this opportunity gaining traction: revenues reached a record $1.9 billion, up 26% year over year, while gross margin expanded to 16.8% from 12% and net income attributable to Amkor rose to $174 million from $54 million.
Growth prospects are increasingly tied to AI/HPC and advanced packaging. Amkor has active programs spanning 2.5D, high-density fan-out and co-packaged optics, while a new data-center CPU program began ramping in the second quarter and is expected to scale through the second half. Computing revenues rose 20% sequentially in the second quarter and were expected to increase nearly 30% sequentially in the third quarter, driven by AI data-center demand and the HDFO CPU ramp. Automotive & Industrial revenues advanced 17% sequentially, with ADAS the primary growth driver.
Strategic customer agreements strengthen the opportunity. A 10-year advanced-packaging agreement with TSMC is designed to expand U.S. packaging and test capacity, while a multi-year NVIDIA partnership targets next-generation AI infrastructure. Amkor expects a $1.5 billion NVIDIA-related customer prepayment in 2027, with services expected to extend roughly five to 10 years. Its Arizona facility is intended to provide high-volume advanced packaging and test capacity in the United States, while expansions in Korea, Vietnam, Portugal and Taiwan increase geographic flexibility.
However, investors should weigh these opportunities against Amkor's semiconductor cyclicality, heavy capital requirements, customer concentration, supply-chain and memory constraints, intense OSAT competition and dependence on sustained AI/HPC packaging demand. The company spent $688 million on capital expenditures in the first half and expects $2.5-$3 billion for 2026. Therefore, a slowdown in AI infrastructure investment could lead to excess capacity, lower utilization and pricing pressure.
AXT is benefiting from strong demand for compound-semiconductor substrates as AI data centers increase their use of high-speed optical connectivity. In the second quarter of 2026, revenues surged 164.8% year over year to $47.6 million, while GAAP gross margin expanded to 44.9% from 8% and GAAP net income reached $11.1 million, versus a $7 million loss a year earlier. Substrate revenues rose 232.7% to $37.6 million, driven primarily by InP demand for data centers and passive optical networks.
The strongest opportunity is indium phosphide (InP), which is emerging as the company's primary growth driver. Second-quarter InP revenues reached a record $30.7 million, while backlog exceeded $100 million. Management said customer demand continues to outpace supply and expects InP revenue opportunity to more than triple by year-end 2026. AXT is doubling InP capacity in 2026, plans another major expansion in 2027 and is progressing toward 6-inch InP substrates, which can support higher-value applications. Demand is being driven by 800G/1.6T transceivers and longer-term co-packaged optics.
AXT has recently deepened relationships with key optical-component customers supporting AI data-center connectivity. It has secured supply agreements with Casela and Coherent and a long-term capacity reservation agreement with Lumentum. These agreements provide greater revenue visibility, validate strong customer demand and support AXT's capacity expansion.
Despite AXT's strong growth prospects, its outlook remains exposed to several operational and geopolitical risks. The company manufactures its wafer substrates in China, making its business vulnerable to changing export controls, tariffs and trade restrictions. Notably, China's export-permit requirement for InP wafers remains a significant concern and can affect the timing of shipments and revenue recognition. AXT also faces semiconductor demand cyclicality, customer order volatility and the risk that major customers reduce, delay or cancel orders. In addition, maintaining high wafer yields and meeting stringent customer specifications are critical, as quality issues can lead to product returns, lower orders and higher manufacturing costs.
How Does the Zacks Consensus Estimate Compare for AMKR & AXTI?
The Zacks Consensus Estimate for AMKR's 2026 and 2027 revenues stands at $7.64 billion and $8.55 billion, respectively, giving Amkor a significantly larger revenue base than AXT. The consensus mark for AMKR's 2026 and 2027 earnings is pegged at $2.60 and $2.72 per share, implying growth of 73.3% and 4.3%, respectively. The earnings estimates have remained stable over the past seven days.
In comparison, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for AXTI's 2026 and 2027 revenues stands at $217.6 million and $453.6 million, respectively. The consensus mark for AXTI's 2026 and 2027 earnings is pegged at 86 cents and $2.20 per share, indicating 309.8% and 155.8% growth, respectively. AXTI's earnings estimates have also remained unchanged over the past seven days.
AMKR vs. AXTI: Price Performance & Valuation Check
AMKR has outpaced AXTI over the past month, with its shares gaining 9.8% compared with a 7.7% rise for AXTI, reflecting stronger recent momentum.
From a valuation perspective, AMKR appears more attractively valued than AXTI. Amkor carries a more favorable Zacks Value Score of B, compared with AXTI's value score of F. AMKR also trades at a forward 12-month price-to-sales ratio of 1.6X, significantly below AXTI's 12.26X.
Amkor and AXT are both positioned to benefit from growing AI infrastructure spending, with AMKR benefiting from advanced packaging demand and AXTI from strong InP substrate demand for optical connectivity. AMKR's growth is supported by expanding AI/HPC packaging programs, strategic partnerships and capacity expansion across key manufacturing locations. AXTI, meanwhile, has a strong InP growth opportunity, supported by record revenues, a growing backlog and capacity expansion plans, but remains more exposed to external factors, including geopolitical and customer-related risks.
However, Amkor's stronger revenue scale, more diversified business, favorable valuation and solid earnings outlook make it a better pick for investors than AXTI, though both stocks sport a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) at present.

Amkor Technology Announces Phase 2 of Arizona Advanced Packaging and Test Campus; Expands Investment to $12 Billion
Strong customer commitments support 60,000 square meter expansion of U.S. advanced packaging capacity
TEMPE, Ariz.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Sep. 8, 2026--
Amkor Technology, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMKR), a leading provider of outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services, today announced phase 2 of its Arizona Advanced packaging and test campus. Driven by strong customer commitments that have surpassed the 33,000 square meters of cleanroom capacity planned for phase 1, the phase 2 expansion is expected to add 60,000 square meters and bring the campus to approximately 93,000 square meters of cleanroom space. The expansion increases the project’s planned investment to approximately $12 billion.
Designed from the outset as a multi-phase project, Amkor’s Arizona campus, which includes wafer bump, probe, assembly and test capabilities, is being developed to support long-term demand for advanced semiconductor packaging and test services in the U.S. Phase 2 expands manufacturing scale, and together with phase 1 is expected to support a workforce of more than 3,500 Arizona-based employees.
“This next phase reflects the confidence our customers have placed in Amkor, the critical role advanced packaging plays in enabling the future of semiconductor innovation, and the strategic importance of our Arizona campus,” said Kevin Engel, president and chief executive officer of Amkor Technology. “As chip architectures become more complex, customers need a trusted partner that can deliver at scale with the quality, technology leadership and operational discipline required for their most advanced products, and it is critical to have that capacity in the U.S.”
Amkor’s Arizona campus is the first OSAT production site in the U.S. for advanced packaging in high volume, giving customers access to a full domestic turnkey manufacturing platform. Construction of phase 2 is anticipated to begin late 2027, with completion expected by the end of 2029. Amkor’s Arizona 170-acre campus allows for further expansion as needed to support customer demand.
